title: Kallanai: a 2,000-year-old dam of uncut stones, still in use
hook_type: You + cement vs only stones + how?
send_test: the engineer friend who thinks old means weak (and anyone from Trichy/Thanjavur)
caption:
Kallanai dam (Grand Anicut), Tamil Nadu: built of uncut stones across the Kaveri by King Karikala Chola around the 2nd century, and still in use today. India Built This #2.

The trick: huge unhewn boulders sunk into the sandy riverbed, in running water. 329 m long, 20 m wide, 5.4 m high.

Extra: in 1804 British engineer J.L. Caldwell raised its stones by 69 cm, and Arthur Cotton later modelled his Lower Anicut on Kallanai. It is counted as the world's fourth-oldest water-regulating structure still in use.

Old stone or modern concrete: which lasts longer? Comment one.
